audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Tryndamere Levels 2, 3, first item and 2+ items, but the prose says the opposite from Level 3 onward — content.mid opens 'From level 3 onward you control this lane' and whys[6] calls the late 1v1 'unwinnable for him'.
audit.why: Six of seven rows disagree with the packet read (Tryndamere / Skill / Swain / Swain / Swain / Swain / Swain), and the packet read matches every why-text on the page plus the 55.56% win rate. Level 1 is genuinely his — crit autos and Bloodlust beat a Q-only Swain — and the page already says so.
audit.corrected: Chart moved to the packet read as matched full/content pairs, with ratings on every row that changed owner. No mirror audit exists for this pair yet.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid states Undying Rage is 'a long 110-second cooldown at rank 1'.
audit.why: It is 120/100/80. The page's whole trading model is 'commit when Undying Rage is down', so a player counting 110 steps in ten seconds early against a champion who is unkillable for the duration — the single worst moment to be wrong in this matchup. The rank-3 figure of 80 also matters, because the window shrinks by a third as the game goes on and the page never says so.
audit.corrected: 120 seconds at rank 1, falling to 80 at rank 3.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout does not appear anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Tryndamere lets out an insulting cry, decreasing surrounding champions' Attack Damage. Enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced.' It reaches 850 on a flat 14s. The slow is conditional on facing — turning to run is what triggers it. For a champion with no dash whose ultimate needs him to hold 650 range, that is the single most actionable fact in the matchup: disengage while facing him and the slow never applies.
audit.corrected: Mocking Shout slows only targets with their backs turned, from 850 on a flat 14s — walk out facing him.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spinning Slash is written as a vague 'spin' and 'spin charge' with no range or cooldown, and spikes[3] miscapitalises it as 'spinning Slash'.
audit.why: Spinning Slash is 650 range on 12/11/10/9/8. Against Nevermove at 850 and Death's Hand at 750, knowing he closes exactly 650 per cast on a 12-second timer at rank 1 is what makes 'only commit if he has no spin' a decision instead of a vibe.

report[8] and dosFull[1] already make anti-heal core, which covers the flagged needs-antiheal interaction on Bloodlust. whys[0] now also carries Bloodlust's flat 12s and the wounded-AD scaling so the player knows what the healing is attached to.
Both packet suspectNames — 'Use Spinning Slash' and 'Pop Undying Rage' — are false positives, correct names preceded by a verb and flagged only by edit distance.

edits.before: From level 3 onward you control this lane. Your W-into-E pattern is the core: drop Vision of Empire at his feet so the slow roots him in place, then launch Nevermove into the rooted body — the pull chains directly into your Q burst and he cannot spin out of the E root. Trade around Undying Rage cooldowns religiously: when it is up, give him nothing and poke from W range; when it is down (a long 110-second cooldown at rank 1), run the full combo and force a back or a kill. Level 6 is your clearest spike — bait his Undying Rage with a shallow R activation, then drain the full five seconds through it; his crit autos barely dent your healing, and Demonflare after it expires deals nova damage while he has no safety net.
edits.after: From level 3 onward you control this lane. Your W-into-E pattern is the core: drop Vision of Empire at his feet so the slow holds him in place, then launch Nevermove into the slowed body — the pull chains directly into your Q burst and he cannot spin out of the root. Trade around Undying Rage religiously: when it is up, give him nothing and poke from W range; when it is down — 120 seconds at rank 1, falling to 80 — run the full combo and force a back or a kill. Level 6 is your clearest spike: bait his Undying Rage with a shallow R activation, then drain straight through it; his crit autos barely dent your healing, and Demonflare after it expires lands while he has no safety net.

notes: Two things carried real risk here. The 110-second Undying Rage cooldown in content.mid is 120/100/80, and a player ten seconds early into an unkillable window dies for it. And Mocking Shout appeared nowhere on the page despite being the ability that punishes Swain's only disengage — its slow applies solely to targets with their backs turned, so the correct instruction is to walk out facing him. No mirror audit exists for tryndamere__swain; whoever runs Tryndamere should take the facing-conditional slow and the chart shape from this file. Left alone: the repeated 'five seconds' duration for Undying Rage. Riot's text gives no duration and I could not verify it, so I neither removed it nor built new advice on it.
